entity.name: Ashiq Hussain Mir
entity.description: Solo maintainer of Canvix, a free and open-source graphic design platform, and a final-year computer-science student based in Jammu & Kashmir, India. Building Canvix full-time around classes since September 2026: 160+ commits, 156 test files (1,575 unit tests plus a 39-file Playwright end-to-end suite) and a live public deployment at canvix.app, all MIT-licensed. Requesting a six-month runway to deliver a design-output correctness, reproducible design-evaluation and creator-education program — a scope deliberately distinct from the pending NLnet application (deployment trust, collaboration scaling, mobile editing, sharing and v1.0 stabilization), so that no hour or deliverable is funded twice.

projects.name: Canvix
projects.description: Free and open-source graphic design platform — a self-hostable, browser-based editor with a 366-template library, real-time collaboration, and local exports to PNG, JPG, SVG, vector PDF, PPTX, GIF and video. MIT-licensed: every feature free, no watermarks, no paywalls, and try-without-account. The AI layer is modular and provider-independent (text, vision, image and video capability slots with bring-your-own-key), and AI-assisted designs remain native, editable elements rather than flattened images — so machine help still produces real design work. One-command Docker self-hosting makes it infrastructure any school, nonprofit or small organization can run itself. This grant funds design-output correctness (exact text and colors, reliable geometry), reproducible design-quality evaluation, and open creator education for the next six months.

plans.name: Milestone 1 — Baseline & evaluation harness (Month 1)
plans.description: Publish the design-quality evaluation plan and a corpus of 20+ diverse briefs; record the current baseline with rendered screenshots, exact text/color comparisons and geometry analysis; set up the dedicated cross-browser test bench; open the public issue tracker and publish the first monthly progress report. Acceptance: evaluation plan, brief corpus, baseline report and tracker are live in the repository.

plans.name: Milestone 2 — Design-output correctness (Months 2–3)
plans.description: Improve brief-to-design constraint handling: verified exact text and color preservation, reliable native editable-element generation, deterministic layout and geometry checks, and reproducible browser tests. Acceptance: the brief-contract suite runs in CI, and every failure documented in the Milestone 1 baseline is fixed with published before/after evidence.

plans.name: Milestone 3 — Grounded visual review (Months 4–5)
plans.description: Reliable comparison of requested versus actual design elements, screenshot-based inspection where a vision model is available, explicit fallback behavior when it is not, and prevention of invented-element claims in completions. Acceptance: public before/after evaluation results across the brief corpus, every verification claim backed by captured evidence, and documented remaining limitations.

plans.name: Milestone 4 — Community, release & final report (Month 6)
plans.description: Release the evaluation toolkit openly; ship user documentation and tutorials plus contributor-onboarding material; hold at least two public community updates or online engagements across the grant period; publish final milestone evidence, a transparent expenditure summary and the final report. Acceptance: toolkit, documentation and final report are public; engagements have happened and are linked.
